catalog_entry.label: All-Star Game and Home Run Derby events
catalog_entry.target: Result or player/event stat in the All-Star Game or Home Run Derby exhibition (winner, hits, HR, strikeouts, derby round totals, longest HR, exit velocity).
catalog_entry.mechanism: Both events are exhibitions generated by who participates and how they are used, not by season-long roles. In the game, selection and withdrawal define the pool, managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers, and the year's rules set length and tiebreaks, so a few plate appearances per player yield rare-event counts shifted by host park and weather. In the Derby, an eight-player self-selected field hits in timed rounds, so homers equal swings times per-swing HR rate with bonus time as feedback, and longest-homer and exit-velocity series are tail extremes.

inputs.why: Participation gate for every player market: appearance, slot and innings determine PA or batters faced.
Year-specific innings, extra-inning or swing-off rule fixes the event window and winner-tie handling.
Field membership and seeding drive qualifier, matchup and finalist markets.
Swings per round and bonus time turn power into round totals and advancement.
Tail model for longest homer, 500 ft count and highest exit velocity.
League talent plus exhibition usage give the winner and MVP-conditioned structure.
Selection rules and vote phases determine who is on the roster pool for player markets.
Barrel, fly-ball and pull-air rate give per-swing and per-PA HR rates for ASG and Derby.
Bat speed and squared-up rate indicate raw power ceiling for derby tails and early-season hitters.
Host park HR factor and ball carry shift ASG HR counts and Derby distances.
Sector-level carry in the host park gives HR probability by batted-ball direction.
Wind along pull side changes HR odds in the ASG and distances in the Derby.
Temperature and altitude carry effect on distances, small but systematic for 500 ft tails.
Roof open or closed at host park removes or restores wind effect on the event.
Strikeout rate and whiff of the arms that pitch one inning each drive ASG strikeouts.
Starter versus reserve status maps to expected PA in a rotating-substitution exhibition.
Regular-season PA-by-slot numbers need replacing by exhibition PA counts; kept as a reference.
Handedness effect applies only mildly because pitchers rotate rather than match up deliberately.
Late scratches and withdrawals change participation and replacements before the event.
League-wide hitter strength of each roster informs winner market relative strength.
Shared game-day HR environment causes overdispersion in total ASG HR.
Past HR/FB luck regression gives per-swing HR probabilities for season-stat-based power.
Roster, pitcher and Derby announcements and refusals arrive via reports before official lists.
Extreme-velocity logic is reused for the highest exit velocity tail in the Derby.
No rules text was sampled; settlement of every ASG and Derby series is unverified.
Official game and Derby results with distances and exit velocities as settlement truth.

interactions.hypothesis: A hitter's expected ASG homers equal his chance of appearing times his expected PA times a small per-PA HR rate, so a power hitter on the bench contributes little while a starter contributes by a PA count that a regular-season lineup slot would overstate.

Bonus time is only triggered by homers beyond a distance threshold, so hitters whose distance distribution crosses it often gain extra seconds and then extra swings, producing a convex jump in round totals above a power cut.

Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.

If a tiebreak swing-off or extra frames can occur and their homers count toward totals, the HR total is a mixture over regimes with a right tail; if they do not count, only nine innings matter and dispersion falls.

contract.settlement_definition: No rules text was sampled for any All-Star Game or Home Run Derby series (all TITLE_ONLY). From titles: the game winner, hits, homers and strikeouts settle on the single exhibition game; Derby series settle on rounds (qualifiers, finals, round-1 leader), HR totals and over/unders, longest homer, 500+ ft homer count and highest exit velocity. Treatment of extra innings or a tiebreak swing-off, void if a player does not appear, and the source of distance and exit-velocity data are not stated and are not inferred here.
variants_and_edge_cases: Player-prop series (KXMLBASGHIT, KXMLBASGHR, KXMLBASGKS) may require appearance; DNP treatment is unknown, CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
Total HR in the All-Star Game (KXMLBALLSTARHR) may or may not include tiebreak swing-off homers.
Derby thresholds (500+ ft, over/under HR, highest exit velocity) depend on official measurement source and tie resolution at reported precision.
Derby qualifier, semifinal and final markets depend on replacements named after listing and on how a swing-off tie is settled.
KXMLBASGMVP is a title for the All-Star Game MVP; MVP is awarded by a selection panel, not by a stat, so settlement rests on the official award.
contract.settlement_data_source: Presumed: official MLB game box score and MVP announcement for the ASG; MLB/Statcast Derby data for HR counts, distance and exit velocity. No rules text names a source (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

mechanism.summary: All-Star Week outcomes come from two exhibition processes with no standings stakes. In the game, a pool of selected players is cut by acceptance and withdrawal, the two managers rotate starters, reserves and one-inning pitchers by convention, and the rule regime for the year fixes length and tiebreaks; a handful of plate appearances per player then produces hits, homers and strikeouts as rare-event counts shifted by host park and weather. In the Derby, a self-selected field of eight hitters hits in timed rounds, so homers equal swings times per-swing HR rate with bonus time as feedback, and longest-homer or exit-velocity markets are extremes of hitter tails. Participation, not talent, is the dominant uncertainty.

stages.name: Selection, acceptance and withdrawal
stages.description: Rosters come from fan vote phases, player ballots and commissioner fill; Derby participants come from invitations that stars often decline. Between announcement and event, injuries and personal choices remove players and replacements enter. The state at market snapshot therefore mixes confirmed and unconfirmed participants. Qualifier and Selections series settle on this stage alone, and every player prop is conditional on it.
stages.distribution: Binary membership per player with correlated late changes; withdrawal hazard rises near the event date.

stages.name: Exhibition usage plan
stages.description: Two managers fill a card with starters, then rotate reserves; pitchers each throw about one inning in a planned order. This determines PA per hitter (zero to about three or four) and batters faced per arm. The format year decides extra innings versus tiebreak and mound limits. The process is closer to a roster allocation problem than to a regular-season lineup.
stages.distribution: Discrete PA counts with many zeros and ones; pitcher batters faced concentrated at 3-5; regime shifts by year.

stages.name: Per-PA outcomes in the exhibition
stages.description: Given a PA, the hit, HR or strikeout chance depends on the hitter's contact and power profile and the arm's whiff and HR vulnerability, with hitters swinging freely and pitchers throwing at maximum effort for one inning. Host park and weather shift HR probability multiplicatively. Because PA counts are tiny, outcomes are rare-event Bernoulli draws with large relative variance.
stages.distribution: Low-count Bernoulli/Poisson-binomial; HR rate small per PA, so zero-inflated totals.

stages.name: Team score, winner and shared-day dispersion
stages.description: Runs and HR aggregate over both teams' exposures; a common day-level factor (wind, ball, pitcher usage) correlates HR counts across the game. The winner follows from run totals and any extra-frame or tiebreak rule. MVP credit goes to a player on the winning side with an outstanding event, which couples the winner market and player stats.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed team and HR totals; winner near coin-flip with league talent a mild tilt; MVP heavy-tailed credit.

stages.name: Derby bracket and round throughput
stages.description: Eight hitters are seeded; timed rounds produce HR counts equal to swings times HR per swing, with bonus time for long homers. Pitcher pace, timeouts and fatigue across three rounds, plus tiebreak swing-offs, determine advancement. Round totals, over/under HR, round-one leader and finalist markets settle on this stage.
stages.distribution: Count per round roughly Poisson with overdispersion from clock and bonus feedback; round-to-round correlation positive within player.

stages.name: Derby extremes: distance and exit velocity
stages.description: Longest homer, 500+ ft count and highest exit velocity are order statistics of hundreds of swings. They depend on each hitter's tail rather than mean, on air carry at the host park and on the number of swings he gets, so they correlate with s5 but follow a heavy-tailed law.
stages.distribution: Generalized Pareto/Gumbel-type tails; discrete 500+ counts; ties possible at reported precision.

talent_strength.note: League and roster strength for the winner market, individual power and strikeout talent for props.

opponent_matchup.note: Matchups are weak because pitchers rotate one inning each; only arm quality and handedness matter, plus Derby pitcher pairing.

role_personnel.note: Rosters, starters, reserves and the Derby field define who is exposed to events.

availability_news.note: Withdrawals, late replacements and participation announcements.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers of the prior pennant winners set lineup order and pitcher rotation by convention; encoded as substitution patterns.

environment.note: Host park, wind, density and roof affect HR counts and distances.

game_context_script.note: No stakes, rotating substitutions and a tiebreak rule shape the score path.

pace_volume.note: PA and batters faced in the ASG; swings and clock in the Derby.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-swing and per-PA HR and hit conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Tail of distance and EV, overdispersed total HR on a single day.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: The exhibition has no standings stakes; fatigue and the Sunday starter exclusion are folded into participation, so no separate schedule or motivation input is needed.

officiating_rules.note: Rule regime for tiebreak, innings and Derby timing and bonus structure.

settlement_contract.note: No rules text was sampled; what counts as a Derby HR and whether tiebreak homers count is unresolved.

mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.label: All-Star Game roster, starters and planned participation (who plays, in which slot, for how many innings)
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.mechanism: Each hitter's plate appearances and each pitcher's batters faced in the exhibition are set by roster composition, the two managers' substitution habits and the announced pitching order, not by a season-long role.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.rationale: A player who is named but enters in the 6th inning gets one or two PAs; a starter gets two or three. Pitchers are normally used for one inning each, so strikeouts come from many arms facing a few batters. Withdrawn players are replaced by commissioner picks, which changes both pool and slots. Every per-player ASG market is first a participation question.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.measurement: Per ASG year 2012-2025 build a table of plate appearances by lineup slot (starter vs reserve entry inning) and batters faced by pitcher role (starter, middle, closer-type). Estimate P(plays at all | selected, position, reserve status) and E[PA | plays] by league/manager, shrunk to the 14-year pooled mean with k = 3 games. For the target year use the posted rosters, listed starters and probable pitchers as of the market timestamp; refresh at lineup announcement (about 1-2 hours before first pitch). Output per player: P(any PA), PA distribution over {0,1,2,3,4}; per pitcher: P(pitches), expected BF.
free_sources: MLB Stats API all-star game feed (free)
raw_data: asg box score: player, team, entry inning, PA, AB, H, HR, K, BF, IP by year
roster announcements with timestamps, withdrawals and replacements
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.why: Hits, HR and strikeout contracts and the MVP are conditional on appearing; participation is the dominant source of variance and zeros in this event.

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.label: All-Star Game format and tiebreak regime for the year (innings, extra-inning or swing-off rule, pitcher limits)
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.mechanism: The rulebook for the year decides how long the exhibition lasts if tied and whether the tiebreak produces countable events.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.rationale: The exhibition has used different tie rules (ghost-runner extras, a derby-style swing-off) and different mound limits across years, so history from an older regime gives wrong total-HR and winner distributions. Whether tiebreak homers count in an All-Star Game HR total is a settlement question and is not known from the title-only series.
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Record per year: scheduled innings, extra-inning rule (automatic runner or not), tiebreak mechanism if any, pitch-count or innings limits, DH use in both leagues, roster size. Encode as categorical regime flags; reweight historical games by regime similarity (weight 1 for same regime, 0.4 otherwise). Collect the commissioner's announcement of rule changes before the event and flag any change announced after market open. P(tie after 9) taken from 14 years of scores as a prior around 0.05-0.10, to be checked.
free_sources: MLB press releases and official ASG rules notes (free_scrape)
MLB Stats API game rules fields (free)
raw_data: per-year ASG rule notes and final scorelines by inning
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.why: Fixes the event window for hits/HR/strikeout totals and decides what a tie means for the winner market.

mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.label: Home Run Derby field: who is invited, who accepts, withdrawal and replacement hazard, seeding
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.mechanism: The Derby field is a self-selected set of hitters, so qualifier and winner markets depend on acceptance, injury withdrawals and replacement choices.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.rationale: Top sluggers often decline, and replacements arrive days before the event. The field is therefore both an input (power distribution of participants) and a target (Selections, Finals Qualifiers). Seeding by season HR or committee changes who meets whom in round 1.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.measurement: For each year 2015-2025 record the invited list at announcement dates, acceptance, final eight, replacements and seeding rule. Model P(accept | rank in season HR, prior participation, age, team home park hosting, injury status) as a logistic with shrinkage k = 5 per feature group. As-of: use announcements dated before the market snapshot; late replacement flagged separately. Output: P(player in final eight) and the seed table.
raw_data: derby participants with announcement dates, replacements, seeding by year
season HR to date at announcement
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.why: Qualifier, finalist and matchup markets cannot be priced without a probability distribution over who is actually in the bracket.

mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.label: Home Run Derby round throughput: swings per minute, bonus-time thresholds, pitcher pace and fatigue across rounds
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.mechanism: In a timed round HR count equals swings taken times P(HR per swing), with bonus time earned by long homers extending the clock.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.rationale: The same power hitter produces very different totals depending on batting-practice pitcher pace, number of timeouts allowed, how often he waits for his pitch, and how much a 3-minute round tires him by the final. Bonus time makes distance a volume input, creating a feedback between power and swings.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.measurement: From Statcast derby data (2015-2025) compute per participant-round: HR, swings, minutes used, bonus seconds earned, timeouts used, mean distance. Model HR per round = swings x p_swing, with swings ~ clock / seconds-per-swing (pitcher-specific, random effect) and p_swing from the hitter's season barrel rate and maximum-EV percentile shrunk to the derby-pooled mean with k = 40 swings. Add fatigue as a multiplicative decay per round (estimate from rounds 1 to 3, shrunk). Rules for bonus (distance threshold, seconds) are taken from the current-year rulebook. As-of: season stats through the Derby date minus one day.
free_sources: Baseball Savant Statcast Home Run Derby data (free_limited)
raw_data: derby swing-level log: participant, round, time, swing result, distance, exit velocity, launch angle, bonus time awarded
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.why: Drives round totals, over/under HR counts, round leader and who advances.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.label: Derby extremes: probability of 500+ foot homers, longest homer and peak exit velocity over the event
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.mechanism: Longest-HR, 500+ ft count and highest exit velocity are maxima of batted-ball distributions over a few hundred swings, so they live in the upper tail of each hitter's power distribution.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.rationale: A batter's average HR distance says little about whether he reaches 500 ft in the event. Tail behaviour needs the hitter's top-decile EV and distance in batting practice and games, the park and wind carry, and the number of swings he gets. Extreme-value logic also makes ties and rounding at the reported distance relevant.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.measurement: For each hitter fit a generalized Pareto tail to HR distances and exit velocities above his own 85th percentile over 3 seasons of Statcast (min 25 exceedances, else borrow league shape and use own scale shrunk with k = 15). Convert park-and-weather effect using the sector-level carry factor from mlb.park_specific_xhr (feet of distance per mph of tailwind and per 10 percent air-density change). Simulate the field's swings from the throughput model and take the maximum per event; report P(any >= 500 ft), P(each hitter has longest), P(max EV > threshold). As-of: games through the previous day.
free_sources: Baseball Savant Statcast batted-ball distance and EV (free)
raw_data: statcast batted balls: batter, hit_distance_sc, launch_speed, launch_angle, park, game_date
derby historical longest HR and max EV by year
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.why: These contracts settle on one extreme value, where mean power and tail power are different things.

mlb.all_star_game_event_model.reason: Targets the same exhibition winner/MVP structure; needs the participation and tiebreak inputs added beneath it.

mlb.all_star_selection_model.reason: Determines the pool from which participants are drawn; relevant mostly to Selections and qualifier series, indirect for game props.

mlb.hitter_hr_profile.reason: Barrel, fly-ball and pull-air rate are the base per-swing and per-PA HR driver for both ASG and Derby.

mlb.bat_tracking.reason: Bat speed marks power ceiling, which matters for derby extremes more than for the single-PA ASG props.

mlb.hr_environment.reason: Park HR factor and ball carry matter for both HR totals; secondary to participation and swings.

mlb.park_specific_xhr.reason: Sector-level carry of the host park is used to adjust the distance tail and HR probability.

mlb.wind_vector_park.reason: Wind along the pull side matters on the event day, but only if the roof is open.

mlb.air_density.reason: Small systematic distance effect; dominated by hitter tail and swing count.

mlb.roof_state.reason: Gates the weather inputs at retractable-roof hosts; not informative elsewhere.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Strikeout and whiff of the one-inning arms drive ASG strikeouts; opposing lineup part of the input is unknowable until lineup posting.

mlb.playing_time_role.reason: Starter versus reserve status approximates expected PA, but needs the ASG-specific plan overriding it.

mlb.expected_pa.reason: Regular-season PA by lineup slot does not transfer to a rotating exhibition; replaced by the ASG participation plan.

mlb.platoon.reason: Handedness effect exists but pitchers are not chosen to match hitters, so weight is low.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: Late scratches change roster and replacement; relevant mostly through the participation gate.

mlb.hitter_quality.reason: Roster-level hitting quality informs the winner market only mildly because of rotating usage.

mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.reason: Day-level latent HR environment creates overdispersion in total ASG HR.

mlb.hrfb_regression.reason: Regression of HR/FB luck is useful for a season sample but adds little over barrel-based profile for single-PA or one-round outcomes.

mlb.news.reason: Reports on participation, replacements and announced pitchers lead official lists.

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.reason: Built for pitch speed extremes; only the extreme-value method transfers to Derby exit velocity, the inputs differ (hitter EV not pitch velocity).

m.rules_text.reason: No rules text is available for these series, so the wording is the largest source of unknown settlement behaviour.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Needed for backtests of results and Derby measurements; settlement data is not an input to a prediction.

interactions.mechanism: A hitter's expected ASG homers equal his chance of appearing times his expected PA times a small per-PA HR rate, so a power hitter on the bench contributes little while a starter contributes by a PA count that a regular-season lineup slot would overstate.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress ASG HR on predicted P(any PA) x E[PA] x season HR rate versus season HR rate alone across 2012-2025 starters and reserves.

interactions.mechanism: Bonus time is only triggered by homers beyond a distance threshold, so hitters whose distance distribution crosses it often gain extra seconds and then extra swings, producing a convex jump in round totals above a power cut.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare round HR totals for hitters above versus below the share of homers over the bonus distance, conditional on swings, in historical derby rounds.

interactions.mechanism: Tailwind, thin air or a short sector shift the distance distribution by a few feet; for a 500 ft threshold in the far upper tail this small shift changes exceedance probability by a large relative amount.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit exceedance counts of 480+ ft in derbies by host-park carry factor and compare slope against median distance slope.

interactions.mechanism: If a tiebreak swing-off or extra frames can occur and their homers count toward totals, the HR total is a mixture over regimes with a right tail; if they do not count, only nine innings matter and dispersion falls.
interactions.how_to_test: Split historical total-HR distributions by rule regime and check the share of games with tail outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: Derby acceptance is correlated with All-Star selection, injury and hosting; a top slugger's refusal moves the replacement's expected power and the whole bracket jointly, not one participant at a time.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate field replacement sequences and test whether a joint acceptance model beats independent acceptance on historical Derby fields.

interactions.mechanism: With the roof closed wind has no effect, with it open wind component along the pull side changes carry; the host park decides which regime is active.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact wind component with a roof-open indicator on historical Derby distances and ASG HR at retractable-roof hosts.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: round HR rises with swings but flattens as fatigue and the clock limit swings
nonlinearities.why: Within a timed round swings are bounded by pitcher pace and hitter fatigue, so extra clock adds fewer homers late in the round and in later rounds.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed (generalized Pareto) response above the hitter's 85th percentile
nonlinearities.why: Extreme markets resolve on the single largest distance or EV, so the mean has little information and the tail shape controls the probability.

nonlinearities.shape: step function: PA counts in {0,1,2,3,4} with large mass at 0 and 1
nonlinearities.why: A rotating exhibition substitutes players by inning, so PA are small integers and hitter outcome distributions are zero-inflated rather than smooth.

catalog_entry.label: Labour stoppage and league season-schedule markets
contract_types: Regular-season games played above a threshold
catalog_entry.target: Whether the MLB regular season starts before a date or plays more than N games, as determined by collective bargaining, any lockout or strike, and the games the league cancels.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The outcome is produced by owner-union collective bargaining after the CBA expires, not by games. Agreement before or after expiry, an owners' lockout decision, hazard of agreement at deadlines (spring training, scheduled opener) and the ramp-up needed after a deal set the first game date; the games played then follow from the schedule after that date and the league's capacity to compress with doubleheaders, with 600 games being a deep-tail threshold against 2,430 scheduled.

inputs.why: Gap between owner and union stated positions governs the chance a deal is reached before games are lost.
Calendar of expiry, report and scheduled opening dates turns bargaining state into dated hazards.
Few comparable stoppages exist, so a reference class gives the prior for stoppage length.
Revenue and cost of waiting for each side determine who concedes and when.
Maps start date to total regular-season games played, including make-up capacity.
CBA expiry date, lockout flag, expected end and transaction freeze rules define the regime.
Scenario table of lockout probability, start and end dates, and games lost under each case.
Reference-class base rate for off-field business events; kept as general prior.
Reports of talks, offers and deadlines arrive before official statements.
Source reliability weights leaks about proposals and sessions when sources conflict.
Official-game and suspended-game rules decide how partially played games count toward games played.
Service-time and roster-freeze rules show what changes during a lockout; indirect effect on bargaining topics.
Transaction timeline shows whether a freeze is on; informative about lockout state only.
Hazards by transaction type are built on team moves; only the calendar idea transfers.
Payroll and tax position indicates owner demands on cost control.
Free-agent class and arbitration status signal how many players feel urgent pressure.
Exact wording of the first-game and games-played conditions fixes what counts.
Market lifecycle events (halts, rule edits) identify when contract text changes.

interactions.hypothesis: The hazard of agreement in a given week is a baseline deadline hazard scaled by the gap size; the same deadline closes a small gap with high probability and a structural gap (such as a cap demand) with low probability, so the effect of a deadline depends on how wide the gap is.

Games lost per day of delay are small until the first regular-season date, then rise at the schedule density; beyond a late-date point the league cancels rather than compresses, so the slope changes at the compression limit.

The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.

Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBOPENINGDAY settles Yes if the first game of the 2027 MLB regular season has taken place before May 31, 2027. KXMLBSEASONGAMES settles Yes if the number of MLB regular-season games played in 2027 is above 600 (strike type greater, floor 600). The sampled rules do not define whether suspended, shortened or tiebreak games count, whether postponed games count at completion, nor name a data source.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first game in the 2027 MLB regular season has taken place prior to May 31, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Condition is the date of the first regular-season game, not the scheduled date; a lockout delaying the opener past May 30 resolves No.

rules_evidence.quote: If the number of MLB regular season games played is above 600 games in the 2027 MLB regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Strict greater-than threshold on total games played league-wide; far below 2,430 scheduled games, so only a near-cancelled season resolves No.

variants_and_edge_cases: The opener series settles on when the first game occurred, not when it was scheduled; if a lockout moves the opening to May 30 versus May 31 the date boundary matters and time zone is not stated.
Strike type greater means exactly 600 games resolves No; one rung is sampled and other thresholds may exist for the same series.
Suspended, shortened or tied games and games played in a tiebreaker (Game 163) are not addressed; whether they count as games played is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
A season that begins on time but later suffers a mid-season strike would affect the games-played contract but not the Opening Day contract.
The sampled rules text mentions only the 2027 regular season; a 2027 postseason or spring-training games are outside both contracts.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules. Presumed: official MLB schedule results and the league's game log (MLB Stats API).

mechanism.summary: Neither contract is decided on the field. The outcome is a bargaining process between ownership and the players' union after the collective agreement expires on December 1, 2026: whether a deal precedes expiry, whether owners lock out, how long agreement takes at the deadlines (spring-training reporting, scheduled opener), and then how many games the league can still schedule after the start date through doubleheaders and make-up days. Opening Day before May 31 requires agreement plus a ramp-up period before that date. More than 600 games of 2,430 fails only if roughly three quarters of the season is lost, so it is a deep-tail stoppage question.

stages.name: Bargaining state before and after CBA expiry
stages.description: The agreement expires on December 1, 2026. Before then the owners decide whether to bargain to a deal, accept an extension or prepare a lockout; the union decides whether to authorize a strike. Positions on economic structure (cap, floor, revenue sharing, tax, pre-arbitration pay) set whether a gap exists and its size. The state is dynamic, updated by each session and each public proposal.
stages.distribution: Discrete state (deal, no deal and talks, lockout) with long persistence; gap index changes in jumps at meetings and leaks.

stages.name: Stoppage duration hazard
stages.description: If no deal exists at expiry, the owners may lock out and stay out until costs rise. Hazard of agreement rises at deadlines: spring-training reporting, the scheduled opener, first missed paychecks. Reference classes (1990, 2021-22 and 1994-95 in baseball; NHL and NBA lockouts) show durations from days to a full season. The question is the cumulative probability that agreement lands before the date that permits play by May 31.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed duration with spikes at deadlines; right-censored; very small sample of comparable events.

stages.name: Ramp-up and first-game date
stages.description: After an agreement, players need a ramp-up period (spring training of about 3-4 weeks) and the league needs to publish a revised schedule. The first regular-season game therefore occurs at a lag after the deal that depends on the date and on whether the league shortens the preparation. Opening Day before May 31 requires the deal and ramp-up to fit before that date.
stages.distribution: Deterministic lag with small variance conditional on deal date; discontinuity at late dates where the league may cancel the season instead.

stages.name: Games scheduled and played after the start date
stages.description: Games played equals scheduled games on dates from the start onward plus any compression through doubleheaders and make-up dates, minus games lost to weather. In a one-week delay the league may recover most games; in a three-month delay it cancels a large share. The 600-game threshold compares to the remaining count, so the threshold hits only if the season loses about three quarters of its 2,430 scheduled games.
stages.distribution: Near-deterministic given start date; step losses by series; threshold far below full schedule so mass is concentrated at the full total or a total near zero.

stages.name: Settlement resolution and official count
stages.description: Opening Day resolves on whether the first 2027 regular-season game has taken place before May 31 and the games-played contract resolves on the count of MLB regular-season games above 600. Postponements, suspended games and tiebreakers are matters of official counting. Both depend on the contract text being read precisely.
stages.distribution: Binary on date; integer count near the schedule total; edge cases are rare.

talent_strength.note: Team and player quality do not determine whether owners and the union reach a deal; the outcome is a league-wide bargaining process, not a contest between rosters.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or matchup in a collective bargaining process; the closest analogue is the gap between the two sides' positions, covered under motivation and timeline inputs.

role_personnel.note: Who negotiates: commissioner, owners' committee, union leadership and membership votes.

availability_news.note: Reports of sessions, offers and lockout decisions with source reliability.

coaching_scheme.note: The bargaining strategy of each side (hardline versus incremental, public versus private) plays the role of tactics.

environment.note: Economic environment: revenue, television contracts and finance conditions that set each side's cost of waiting.

game_context_script.note: Expected path of the negotiation over the calendar, from expiry to the scheduled opener.

pace_volume.note: Number of games remaining at a given start date and make-up capacity.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate exists; the outcome is a duration and a schedule count, so the nearest analogue is the hazard of agreement per week under the timeline input.

distribution_variance.note: Heavy-tailed duration distribution and the nearly bimodal count of games played.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Deadlines, paychecks and stakes drive concessions.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league rules on lockout, freeze and schedule revision.

settlement_contract.note: Wording of before-date and above-threshold conditions; some edge cases unresolved.

mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.label: MLB-MLBPA bargaining positions: proposals on the economic system, salary-cap or floor demands, and public statements
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.mechanism: Whether a deal is reached before expiry is set by the gap between owner and union proposals on the economic system and by each side's stated red lines.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.rationale: The sticking points in baseball talks are structural (revenue sharing, payroll limits, luxury-tax design, pre-arbitration pay) rather than incremental. A salary-cap demand by owners against a union that has historically refused any cap produces a hard gap that does not close by small concessions, so stated red lines matter more than the number of meetings.
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.measurement: Code each public proposal or leak by topic (cap/floor, tax thresholds, revenue share, service-time, arbitration, draft, schedule length) as {proposed by, date, source tier}. Compute a gap index = number of topics with incompatible stated positions / topics open, updated at each bargaining session; add a red-line flag when either side calls an item a non-starter. As-of: public reports timestamped before the snapshot; discount single-source leaks to weight 0.5 until confirmed by a second outlet.
raw_data: dated list of proposals by topic and party
statements by commissioner and union leadership with timestamps
mlb.cba_bargaining_positions.why: Opening Day timing and games played are determined by whether the gap closes before or after the expiry and spring-training deadlines.

mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.label: Bargaining calendar hazard: days to expiry, owners' lockout decision date, spring-training and scheduled-opener deadlines
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.mechanism: A deal can only arrive at certain points on a fixed calendar, and the hazard of agreement rises near binding deadlines.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.rationale: The CBA expiry on December 1, 2026 is the first deadline; the second is the February pitchers-and-catchers report date; the third is the scheduled opener. The market threshold date of May 31 and the 600-game strike value sit after all three, so the relevant question is the cumulative hazard through several deadlines, not at one.
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.measurement: Build a discrete-time hazard on weekly steps from expiry to the scheduled opener plus 60 days: h(t) = P(agreement in week t | none yet), with features: weeks to the next hard deadline (spline), lockout in force flag, number of formal sessions in last 14 days, gap index. Fit on 1972, 1973, 1976, 1980-81, 1985, 1990, 1994-95, 2002, 2016 and 2021-22 episodes with strong shrinkage; map to P(first regular-season game before May 31) = P(agreement by the date implied by scheduled opening plus allowed ramp-up (about 3-4 weeks for spring training)). Dates taken from the published schedule and CBA text as of the snapshot.
free_sources: CBA text and prior CBA expiry timeline (free)
raw_data: calendar of deadlines: CBA expiry, report dates, scheduled opening day, break points
historical stoppage episodes with start, end and cancelled games
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.why: Converts a bargaining state into a probability that games start before a given date.

mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.label: Reference class of MLB and comparable league stoppages: duration, cancelled games and ramp-up needed before play
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.mechanism: With very few comparable events the best prior for stoppage length is the historical distribution across baseball and other major leagues, adjusted for how much money is at stake.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.rationale: Only about nine baseball stoppages exist, ranging from a few days to a cancelled postseason, and 2021-22 delayed but did not shorten the schedule. Cross-sport lockouts (NHL 2004-05 lost the season, NBA 2011 lost about 16 games) add a heavy tail the baseball sample alone does not show.
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.measurement: Table of MLB stoppages: type (strike or lockout), start, end, duration in days, regular-season games cancelled, spring training lost, ramp-up days between agreement and first game. Cross-sport table for NHL/NBA/NFL. Fit a mixture: P(short) from MLB (deal before first scheduled game), P(long) from pooled leagues; weight MLB episodes 1.0 and others 0.3; add a Beta prior (a=2, b=2) on P(any regular-season games cancelled). As-of: static history, update for any new episode.
free_sources: Wikipedia and league histories for NHL/NBA lockouts (free)
raw_data: episode table: dates, games lost, ramp-up days
mlb.lockout_precedent_reference_class.why: Gives the base rate for a stoppage reaching May 31 or removing three quarters of the schedule.

mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.label: Leverage state: owners' revenue and broadcast contract position versus players' strike-fund and salary exposure
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.mechanism: A stoppage lasts as long as both sides' costs of waiting stay below their expected gain, which depends on revenue, television contracts, player earnings at risk and reserves.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.rationale: Regional sports network disruptions, national TV renewals and a rising luxury tax change who loses more from lost games. A lockout is a bet that players, who miss paychecks, concede first. Those costs are observable only through proxies, so the input must be built from revenue indicators and public finance data.
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.measurement: Construct a leverage ratio = owners' cost of lost games per week (national media revenue share + gate + local media at risk, from public estimates and league-wide revenue reports) divided by players' cost per week (average salary share of the schedule, with a distribution weighting by arbitration and minimum-salary players) and a strike-fund and reserve indicator for the union. Update quarterly; treat as ordinal (-1, 0, +1) when exact data is missing. As-of: latest annual report or credible estimate before the snapshot.
free_sources: Forbes/Sportico franchise valuations and revenue estimates (free_limited)
MLBPA and league financial disclosures where public (free_limited)
raw_data: league revenue estimates and media contract terms
player payroll by tier, union reserves where disclosed
mlb.owner_union_leverage_state.why: Sets which side is under pressure to settle before games are lost.

mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.label: Schedule map from start date to games played: games per calendar day, scheduled finish date and make-up capacity
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.mechanism: Games played in a shortened season equals scheduled games on dates after the first game, plus any games the league can add through doubleheaders and make-up days.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.rationale: Of the 2,430 scheduled games, the share that remain after a given delay depends on how the schedule is spread (about 13 to 15 games per calendar day on average, with fewer on Mondays and in April) and on whether MLB prefers to compress by doubleheaders, cancel series or play 162 by extending the season. The 600-game strike corresponds to a very late start or season cancellation.
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.measurement: From the published 2027 schedule compute N(d) = scheduled games on or after date d for each d, and D(d) = days until the last scheduled regular-season day. Estimate recoverable games R(d) = min(doubleheader capacity, off days that can be used) with doubleheader capacity = 0.25 x open dates (calibrated on 2021-22, where the full 162 was played after the delay, a compression through a few extra doubleheaders). Predicted games played G(d) = N(d) + R(d), cutoff d* such that G(d*) = 600. As-of: schedule file version at snapshot.
raw_data: schedule by date with games per day
doubleheader and off-day inventory
mlb.games_per_calendar_day_makeup_map.why: Translates stoppage length into games played and Opening Day timing.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.reason: Direct description of the bargaining regime and the CBA expiry; the entire outcome is a function of it.

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.reason: Scenario mapping of lockout length to games lost is the correct form for both contracts, once tied to the schedule map.

mlb.offfield_base_rate.reason: General off-field base rate is too coarse for a CBA expiry; the precedent table replaces it for the core prior.

mlb.news.reason: Bargaining reports lead official statements, and the timeline moves when they appear.

mlb.news_source_reliability_score.reason: Leaks on proposals and offers vary in reliability, so a source weight prevents overreaction.

mlb.game_completion_rules.reason: Only relevant to whether the 600th game count includes suspended or shortened games; second-order here.

mlb.service_time_rules.reason: Service-time rules are a bargaining topic but do not drive stoppage timing as an input beyond a topic flag.

mlb.roster_moves.reason: A transaction freeze is a consequence of a lockout, so it indicates state but does not predict it.

mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.reason: Built for team transactions; the hazard-over-calendar method transfers but the estimates do not.

mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.reason: Team payroll position informs owners' economic demands but is a slow variable.

mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.reason: Individual contract states are too granular; the free-agent class size only matters as a mild leverage signal.

m.rules_text.reason: The two contracts differ in how the date and count are defined, so wording is a first-order input.

m.lifecycle.reason: Useful to detect rule edits or halts; no predictive role.

interactions.mechanism: The hazard of agreement in a given week is a baseline deadline hazard scaled by the gap size; the same deadline closes a small gap with high probability and a structural gap (such as a cap demand) with low probability, so the effect of a deadline depends on how wide the gap is.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit weekly hazard with gap index, deadline proximity and their product on stoppage episodes and test the product term, using the 2021-22 and 1990 cases as holdouts.

interactions.mechanism: Games lost per day of delay are small until the first regular-season date, then rise at the schedule density; beyond a late-date point the league cancels rather than compresses, so the slope changes at the compression limit.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate games played over a grid of deal dates with and without doubleheader capacity and locate the breakpoint where G(d) falls below 600.

interactions.mechanism: The reference class is informative only if the leverage regime resembles the historical episode; when television revenue is guaranteed (owners' cost of waiting lower) long stoppages are more likely than the baseball sample implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition historical durations on a revenue-guarantee indicator across MLB, NHL and NBA episodes and compare tails.

interactions.mechanism: Once a lockout is declared the process moves from a pre-expiry regime where deals are common near the deadline to a lockout regime where only paycheck pressure and calendar deadlines close the gap, so new reports have different weights in each regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate hazards by regime flag and test whether news-dated shifts in agreement odds differ before and after the lockout start.

interactions.mechanism: Opening Day before May 31 needs agreement at least a ramp-up period earlier; the market answer is a step in the deal date, with the step located by the ramp-up length.
interactions.how_to_test: Define deal date minus ramp-up and test historical first-game dates for a step at the ramp-up lag (1990 and 2021-22).

nonlinearities.shape: spiking hazard near hard deadlines (expiry, report date, scheduled opener) and flat between
nonlinearities.why: Concessions concentrate when costs become real, so the probability of agreement is not smooth in time and a constant-hazard model misestimates both short and long stoppages.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise-linear decline in games played with start date, then collapse beyond the compression limit
nonlinearities.why: Early delays can be recovered through doubleheaders, but past a point the league cancels games, so total games played is a nonlinear function of the deal date.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: little effect until a red-line item is declared, then a large drop in near-term agreement probability
nonlinearities.why: Structural disputes such as a salary cap do not close with small concessions, so the gap index matters mainly once it crosses a structural level.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Static history; add new episodes at resolution.
required_data.history_needed: All MLB stoppages since 1972 and NHL/NBA/NFL since 1987.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Schedule version at snapshot; changes recorded.

candidate_sources.name: MLB.com schedule and Stats API schedule endpoint

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Time of first report and confirmation time; market snapshot as-of.
required_data.history_needed: 2021-22 talks and the current negotiation from the start.

unresolved.what_would_resolve: Rules text or operator clarification on the time-zone convention.

catalog_entry.label: Playoff series winner, total games, spread and games hosted
catalog_entry.target: Winner, number of games, game margin of a best-of-N postseason series, or number of playoff games a club hosts.
catalog_entry.mechanism: A series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that differ by game: the bracket sets home pattern, off days compress rotations so each game has a different starter, bullpen fatigue accumulates and resets, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games and spread are functions of the same series score, while games hosted is a path-dependent sum of home games over the rounds reached.

inputs.why: Convolves bracket path, series length and home pattern into the number of home games for a named club.
Starter assignment per game under off-day compression determines per-game win probability.
Accumulated reliever fatigue changes late-series strength and the length of the series.
Round-specific rosters and injury returns change strength between series.
Series state, games played, off days and home-field pattern drive the remaining path.
Elimination and leverage state of the series inform manager decisions in the next game.
Probability of 4, 5, 6, 7 games from game-level win probabilities is the total-games contract.
Exact series score distribution gives winner, game spread and total-games jointly.
Pairing, series length and home-field pattern probabilities define the hosting path and later opponents.
Rating based on top starters, top relievers and the regular lineup suits short series.
Short leash and high-leverage reliever usage compress talent gaps in the playoffs.
Starter true talent feeds the per-game win probability with the assignment table.
Bullpen quality matters more in playoff games as relievers pitch a larger share of innings.
Lineup offence against the handedness of the starters expected in the series.
Injuries before and during the series with point-in-time vintages.
Seeding, byes and tiebreaks define who hosts which game.
Seed state and tiebreakers decide home-field in the bracket; relevant to hosting counts before the bracket is set.
Rotation slot and rest days for each starter before and during the series.
Park-specific home advantage is small but enters the per-game probability and hosting.
Talent prior from projections; weak late in the season but used as shrinkage target.
Playoff odds produce who reaches the series; used for hosting markets before pairings are set.
Plate umpire zone tendencies shift single-game scoring a little.
Series winner, total games and spread wording determines what counts as a game or a margin.
Official series results and number of games as settlement truth.

interactions.hypothesis: An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.

Winner, length and margin share one score distribution; a strong favourite raises sweep probability and lowers the chance of game seven, so total-games and spread markets move in opposite directions as the rating gap grows.
Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.

Hosting 8 or more games requires reaching the pennant or World Series stage as a high seed; the count has a large jump when a club advances from a round, so the probability of 8+ is a step in the number of rounds won.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBSERIES pays Yes if the named club wins the named series; KXMLBSERIESGAMES pays Yes if the total games played exceed the strike (6.5 sampled); KXMLBSERIESSPREAD pays Yes if the club wins by more than the strike in games (3.5 sampled); KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST pays Yes if the club hosts at least the strike number of playoff games (8 sampled). KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL is title only. Sampled rules do not state treatment of suspended or unfinished series or the data source.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tampa Bay wins the Tampa Bay vs Milwaukee Championship Series in the 2026 Pro Baseball Playoffs
rules_evidence.establishes: Winner market is series advancement, independent of game count or margin; the rules name a specific series.

rules_evidence.quote: If more than 6.5 games are played in the Tampa Bay vs Milwaukee Championship Series
rules_evidence.establishes: Total games contract is a half-point over/under on games played, so over 6.5 means a full seven games in a best-of-seven.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tampa Bay wins by more than 3.5 games in the Tampa Bay vs Milwaukee Championship Series
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread is the series margin in games for the winner; above 3.5 requires a margin of 4, which in a best-of-seven means a 4-0 sweep.

rules_evidence.quote: hosts at least 8 playoff games in the 2026 Pro Baseball season
rules_evidence.establishes: Count of home playoff games across all rounds of the season, with an at-least strike (greater_or_equal).

variants_and_edge_cases: Spread above 3.5 is only reachable in a best-of-seven (4-0); in a best-of-five the maximum margin is 3, so the same-form market would settle No structurally.
Total games strike 6.5 is Yes only if the series reaches game seven; the market for a best-of-five or best-of-three series needs different strikes (series length is format-dependent).
Hosting count thresholds interact with the round structure: a wild-card club hosts at most three games in the short first round and none if it is the lower seed.
Suspended games, rain delays or a series that does not finish are not addressed in the sampled rules (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).
KXMLBSERIESGAMETOTAL is title only; whether it differs from KXMLBSERIESGAMES (for example exact count markets) cannot be seen.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules. Presumed: official MLB postseason game results (MLB Stats API / box scores).

mechanism.summary: A playoff series is a first-to-N path through per-game win probabilities that are not identical: the bracket fixes who hosts which game, each game has a different announced starter after off-day compression, relievers accumulate fatigue and reset on off days, and rosters change between rounds. Winner, total games and game spread are three functions of the same final score (for example a margin above 3.5 games in a best-of-seven needs a 4-0 sweep), while playoff games hosted is a path-dependent sum of home games over the rounds a club reaches. Short series compress talent gaps because managers shorten starters' leashes and lean on top relievers.

stages.name: Bracket, seeding and series format
stages.description: The postseason bracket sets who plays whom, in what length (short first round, then longer series), which club is the higher seed and the home pattern per game. Byes and tiebreakers are decided before the first series. For hosting counts this stage also produces the set of rounds a club can reach; for single-series contracts it fixes the best-of-N length and home pattern.
stages.distribution: Discrete bracket paths; deterministic format given seeds; path probabilities driven by upstream series results.

stages.name: Rosters, injuries and round-specific strength
stages.description: Each series has a submitted roster; injured players may return or be replaced between rounds, and key injuries during a series change strength. Team quality is therefore round-specific and uses a playoff-weighted rating (top starters, top relievers, regular lineup) rather than the full season average.
stages.distribution: Discrete roster states with continuous strength shifts; injury arrival roughly Poisson with heavy impact for stars.

stages.name: Starter assignment and rest under off days
stages.description: Postseason schedules have off days, so managers use three or four starters and may use an ace on short rest or a bullpen game. The identity of the starter in each game defines that game's win probability and the series is a sequence of different matchups rather than repeated draws of the same one.
stages.distribution: Categorical starter per game with conditional dependence on prior games; bullpen-game tail.

stages.name: Per-game win probability and bullpen fatigue
stages.description: Given starters, lineups and park, a game is a win-probability draw with a small home edge. Short leashes make the bullpen cover a larger share of innings, and fatigue accumulates across consecutive games, resetting on off days. This couples games within a series: a heavy bullpen game two days ago lowers the next game's strength.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with probability varying by game and weakly correlated across games through shared fatigue.

stages.name: Series dynamic program: winner, length, margin
stages.description: The series result is the first-to-N-wins path through per-game probabilities. Winner, total games and game margin (spread) are functions of the same path; a sweep produces the largest margin and the shortest length. The state at the snapshot (games played, score, elimination) fixes the remaining tree.
stages.distribution: Discrete path distribution over scores 4-0 to 4-3 (or 3-0 to 3-2); lengths 4-7; correlated margins and lengths.

stages.name: Hosting count convolution and settlement
stages.description: For hosted-games contracts the number of home games is the sum over rounds reached of home games in each series played (a function of series length and seed pattern). The contracts settle on official game counts and series results.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent integer sum; support roughly 0-11 for a bye team; tail depends on reaching late rounds.

talent_strength.note: Playoff-weighted team ratings, starters and bullpens.

opponent_matchup.note: Offence versus expected starters and handedness of the specific series.

role_personnel.note: Starters per game and round-specific rosters.

availability_news.note: Injuries and reliever availability inside the series.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager rotation use, leash and leverage deployment.

environment.note: Venue and umpire effects; weather is secondary and dealt with by single-game inputs.

pace_volume.note: Games played in the series and games hosted over rounds.

efficiency_conversion.note: The contracts are decided by game wins, not by a conversion rate of a repeated opportunity; per-game win probability is a composite handled in team rating and starter inputs, with no independent efficiency variable.

distribution_variance.note: Series score and length distributions with game dependence.

officiating_rules.note: Postseason format, series length and extra-inning rules; umpiring is secondary.

settlement_contract.note: Series winner, total games, spread and hosted games wording; open questions about suspended or unfinished series.

mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.label: Playoff games hosted: bracket path, series length and home-game pattern by round for a named club
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.mechanism: Games hosted equals the sum over rounds of home games in each series actually played, so it depends on seed, byes, which rounds are reached and how long each series lasts.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.rationale: A club with a first-round bye can host up to three games in the division series, four in the league championship series and four in the World Series, while a wild-card club hosts at most three in the short first round. The count is therefore a path-dependent random sum with a different home pattern per round (2-2-1, 2-2-1-1-1, 2-3-2), not just a series win probability.
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.measurement: For each club enumerate bracket paths from seed using mlb.bracket_path_enumeration. Per round r: series length L_r from the series-length distribution and home count h_r(L_r, higher seed flag) from the format pattern (higher seed hosts games 1, 2, 5 of the division series; 1, 2, 6, 7 of championship series; World Series by regular-season record). Simulate with 20,000 paths from team-level win probabilities with correlation parameter rho = 0.05 and report P(hosts >= k) for k = 1..11 with Monte Carlo error. As-of: current standings and series state at the snapshot; update after every game.
raw_data: postseason format table: round, length, home pattern by seed
current seeds and results
mlb.playoff_hosting_count_path_model.why: KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST asks for 8+ home games; this input is the path convolution that produces it.

mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.label: Projected starter for each game of the series after off days, with short-rest and bullpen-game probabilities
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.mechanism: Which starter pitches game k depends on the announced rotation, off days, ace usage on short rest and the chance of a bullpen game.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.rationale: In a short series the top starters pitch more games, so team strength is not constant across games. Game 5 of a division series or Game 7 may feature an ace on short rest or an opener. Postseason off days compress the rotation to three or four men, making the per-game win probability a sequence rather than a single number.
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.measurement: For each remaining game build a probability table P(starter = s) from rotation order, days of rest (off days count), number of starts so far, manager history of three- versus four-man rotations (postseason 2015-2025), injuries, and statements by managers (weight 0.5 until announced). Convert to per-game win probability by log5 with starter quality (SIERA/Stuff+ blended with 3-year projection, shrinkage k = 60 IP) plus bullpen-day penalty for P(opener). As-of: announcements through the snapshot time; probables update with each game.
raw_data: probable starters by game with timestamps
pitcher days of rest, innings and pitch counts in series
mlb.series_starter_assignment_by_game.why: Per-game win probabilities in total games, spread and winner markets differ by game because the starter changes.

mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.label: Cumulative bullpen workload across the series: relievers' pitches on consecutive days and off-day resets
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.mechanism: High-leverage relievers cannot pitch every day, so fatigue and unavailability accumulate over games and reset on off days.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.rationale: In a short series managers use the best relievers heavily, which makes the closer's availability in game 5 depend on usage in games 3 and 4 and on the schedule of off days. This is a dynamic availability state, unlike the regular-season rest rules, and it can reduce a stronger team's edge late in the series.
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.measurement: Track reliever pitches in the last 1, 2 and 3 days from play-by-play; flag unavailability when pitches >= 25 yesterday or 3 consecutive days (thresholds from regular-season 2021-25 usage, calibrated per manager, shrunk k = 30 appearances). Compute team leverage-weighted bullpen availability score = sum over relievers of (talent x P(available)), as of the lineup-card time. Reset on off days using the observed usage patterns in postseason series.
raw_data: reliever pitch counts by date, leverage index of entries, off-day calendar
mlb.series_bullpen_cumulative_workload.why: Series total games and winner depend on late-series bullpen state that regular-season averages miss.

mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.label: Postseason roster eligibility between rounds: injured-player replacement, roster resets and who can be on the series roster
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.mechanism: Each series has its own submitted roster, so an injured player may return or be replaced between rounds, which changes team strength round by round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.rationale: A team's strength entering the league championship series is not the same roster as in the division series; hitters and pitchers can be swapped between rounds under league rules. This matters for hosting-count markets that span several rounds and for any series where injuries occur in the previous round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.measurement: For each team log submitted postseason rosters by round (2012-2025), flag injured-list players with return timelines and replacements; compute expected strength change = sum of WAR-above-replacement difference of players added minus removed, using projections (ZiPS/Steamer rest-of-season rates). As-of: roster submission deadline and public injury reports; unconfirmed flagged as probability weights.
free_sources: MLB transactions page and postseason roster announcements (free_scrape)
raw_data: roster submissions per round, injury returns, replacements
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.why: Strength differs between rounds so multi-round markets cannot use a single regular-season roster.

mlb.series_context.reason: Series state and home-field pattern are directly the path variables for all four contracts.

mlb.series_game_state.reason: Elimination state changes managers' pitcher usage in the next game, directly affecting game win probability.

mlb.series_length_distribution.reason: Exactly the total-games contract and, with exact scores, the base for hosting counts.

mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.reason: Gives joint winner, margin and length; the spread contract is a function of the final score.

mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.reason: Needed for hosting counts and for any series not yet set.

mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.reason: Playoff-weighted team rating suits a short series better than full-season ratings.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Usage patterns change who pitches the late innings; second-order next to starter assignment.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Starter talent is an input but only through the assignment table; alone it ignores off-day effects.

mlb.bullpen_talent.reason: Bullpen talent enters as a share of innings; needs availability from the workload input.

mlb.team_wrc_vs_hand.reason: Offence against the specific starters faced is better than overall offence, but effect size is modest.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: Injuries to key players before or during a series move the winner probability directly.

mlb.postseason_seeding_rules.reason: Fixes home-game pattern and byes; static once the bracket is set.

mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.reason: Matters before seeds are final; useless for a series already in progress.

mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.reason: Rotation and rest feed the starter assignment table; partly duplicated by it but kept as the raw input.

mlb.home_field_run_advantage.reason: Small home edge relative to starter variance; matters for hosting and close series.

mlb.preseason_projections.reason: Preseason talent priors are dominated by in-season data and the postseason adjusted rating by October.

mlb.season_sim.reason: Provides probabilities of who reaches each series; irrelevant once the pairing is known.

mlb.umpire.reason: Zone tendencies shift runs per game slightly but have little effect on series outcome and total games.

m.rules_text.reason: Spread wording ('wins by more than 3.5 games') and total-games wording have structural implications that depend on series length.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Official series results and game counts are needed for backtests and settlement checks, not as a predictor.

interactions.mechanism: An ace on short rest or a bullpen game raises the next days' relief usage, so the rotation decision in game k conditions bullpen availability in k+1 and k+2; the effect on win probability is larger when off days are absent.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game bullpen availability on prior starter innings and rest, then compare win probability residuals in postseason games after bullpen days.

interactions.mechanism: Winner, length and margin share one score distribution; a strong favourite raises sweep probability and lowers the chance of game seven, so total-games and spread markets move in opposite directions as the rating gap grows.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate series over a grid of per-game win probability with and without game dependence and compare to historical series score frequencies (1995-2025).

interactions.mechanism: Reliever concentration compresses the benefit of full-season depth; once the top three starters and top relievers account for most innings, adding depth beyond them does not raise win probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rating variants (full roster versus top-heavy weighting) in predicting playoff game outcomes across 2012-2025.

interactions.mechanism: Hosting 8 or more games requires reaching the pennant or World Series stage as a high seed; the count has a large jump when a club advances from a round, so the probability of 8+ is a step in the number of rounds won.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(hosts >= k) conditional on the number of rounds reached and compare against a model that ignores round structure.

interactions.mechanism: Under elimination the trailing manager shortens starters' leash and uses top relievers early, so win probability behaves differently in elimination games than in game one of a series.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact elimination flag with starter innings share and test whether game win probability residuals differ for elimination versus non-elimination games.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in the per-game win probability gap: sweep probability rises faster than linearly as the favourite strengthens
nonlinearities.why: Series outcome is a binomial-type path function, so a small per-game edge becomes a larger series edge and total-games and spread probabilities change nonlinearly.

nonlinearities.shape: step changes in win probability by starter identity, with a tail for bullpen games
nonlinearities.why: The best starter pitches a game with a clearly higher win probability, and a bullpen game lowers it, so per-game strength is multimodal across games.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in rounds reached; integer-valued sum with a jump at each round
nonlinearities.why: Home games are added in blocks by round, so the count is a lumpy function of advancement rather than a smooth variable.
